resources.string: Small steps. A little more breathing room.
Every recorded expense helps fill in the picture.
A gentler pace. Enjoy the little win.
Close to your usual rhythm. One small choice can make a difference.
A busy spending week? Take a breath and check what can wait.
First mission: record your expenses, even the little ones. Your personal goal will appear once there is enough history.
Your latest week already meets this goal. Nice work — keep it comfortable.
Your latest week is %1$s above this goal. Look for a small, optional expense to trim.
A gentle goal: 5% below your usual week. It changes with your habits; this is not a spending allowance.
The 24-hour pause\nBefore your next nonessential purchase, give it a day. Still want it tomorrow?
Your biggest categories. Start with something flexible — essentials come first.

Your daily amount includes everything recorded in the last 7 days.

Keep logging consistently. After at least 5 weeks of history, including earlier spending, there should be enough to discover your usual pace. Until then, the needle stays neutral.

Investments and excluded category shares do not count.

Your pace compares the last 7 days with your usual week from the preceding 4–8 weeks. New expenses count as soon as they are recorded.

Mint: at least 5% below usual.
Amber: near usual, up to just under 15% higher.
Coral: 15% higher or more.

Bills and big purchases can move the needle. This is a guide to your habits, not a judgment or a measure of what you can afford. Missing entries can make the pace look lower. Investments and excluded category shares do not count.
